items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Was this like the T. O. B. A. [Theater Owners' Booking Association]? Like Sammy Davis, Will Mastin, the kind of things they were doing? [INTERVIEWEE] Definitely. No question about it. Peg Leg Bates.

ctx.x: Vaudeville. That’s the term I’m looking for. Thanks, Dave. Vaudeville was still big, [but] it was on the wane. You saw the handwriting on the wall for vaudeville and the whole vaudeville syndrome, but there was [still] a lot of action, a lot of activity. All of the major cities had theaters where you'd have a band, and a big name singer, and an act, and a dog act or animal act, and a comedian. This was vaudeville. They were variety-type shows. This was still very prevalent.
Was this like the T. O. B. A. [Theater Owners' Booking Association]? Like Sammy Davis, Will Mastin, the kind of things they were doing?
Definitely. No question about it. Peg Leg Bates.
